summary: This resolution sets House floor procedures for debating and voting on a fiscal year 2026 continuing appropriations bill and a resolution honoring Charlie Kirk, while moving certain committee deadlines from March 31 to January 31, 2026.

scores.thoughts: The resolution sets procedural rules for House consideration of a continuing appropriations bill (H.R. 5371) but does not itself authorize, expand, reduce, or alter any spending levels or appropriations. It is strictly a rules package and has no substantive effect on government spending.
The bill text contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
No references to healthcare policy, coverage, funding, or regulation appear in the resolution.
The resolution does not address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa-related content is present.
The bill contains no language concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the underlying appropriations bill may touch defense funding, this procedural resolution does not engage with or alter military spending.
No environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions are included.
The resolution does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net funding.
No education policy, school funding, or choice provisions are mentioned.
The text has no bearing on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related matters.
No criminal justice, sentencing, or policing reforms are addressed.
The resolution contains nothing related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
Although appropriations can indirectly relate to deficits, this procedural measure does not engage with debt reduction or deficit policy.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights appear.
The bill does not address foreign assistance or aid programs.
No election administration, voting access, or integrity measures are included.
The resolution has no content related to technology regulation or data privacy.
No labor, union, or worker-protection provisions are present.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination policy.
